notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.38
notes.content:
[p]Hi everyone![/p][p]Today I’m sharing a small update while you’re waiting for the next area to arrive. It includes some new outfits, a few fixes, and quality-of-life improvements.[/p][h3][b]New Content[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Added two new outfits: [b]School Sports Uniform[/b] and [b]School Swimsuit[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]In total, this update adds [b]11 new clothing items[/b], including multiple color variations.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45015378/8b16afc51f749d8f5b2aa4e0e8ea459cd52efd65.png"][/img][/p][list][*][p]A new [b]magazine[/b] has been placed in the [b]Basement Save Room[/b].
Since players often find it earlier than the one in the locker, the [b]sewing tutorial[/b] has also been moved there to better match the progression.[/p][/*][/list][h3][b]Fixes & Improvements[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the character could stand up and attack from a crouching position even when there wasn’t enough space. This should no longer occur.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a few short voice lines to notify you when Ealish can’t stand or attack due to low ceilings or tight spaces.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an item duplication exploit that could occur when using "Place / Store" while the "Move" action was still active.[/p][/*][*][p]Improved [b]gamepad sensitivity settings[/b]. The slider’s maximum value has been increased from 1 to 2, offering more flexibility for players to adjust the controls to their liking.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a new [b]Motion Blur setting[/b] in the [b]Graphics[/b] tab. You can now control how intense the effect is - or turn it off entirely if you prefer a cleaner look.[/p][/*][*][p]The current [b]game version[/b] is now displayed in the [b]Save window[/b] for convenience.[/p][/*][*][p]Expanded the [b]basement storage box[/b] from 16 to 32 slots to better support the growing number of outfit pieces.[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted [b]item drop rates[/b] from zombies to make loot feel more balanced and less overwhelming.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a movement issue that occurred when pressing opposite directional inputs (such as Left and Right) simultaneously.[/p][/*][/list][p]That’s all for now! Thank you so much for your support and patience.[/p][p]Things might be a little quiet for a bit while I focus on developing the next chunk of content, but I’m always reading your feedback — so feel free to share your thoughts.[/p][p]And if you haven’t yet, you’re welcome to join the [url="https://discord.gg/dG7bVqryDQ"]Discord community[/url] to stay in the loop.[/p][p]Thanks again, and see you in the next update!

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.37.4
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

Since there’s only one day left until the Early Access launch, I decided to improve the build tracking system as early as possible.

Over time, I noticed that without proper version tracking, many players could get confused when loading old save files in newer versions of the game. This can lead to bugs and glitches, and it became clear that a better system was necessary to prevent issues like these in the future.

[h3]How this affects you:[/h3]
All save files created before update [b]0.37.4[/b] will now be marked as "[b]Unknown[/b]."
This means that to ensure proper game tracking, you’ll need to start a [b]new game from scratch[/b].
I really didn’t want to make such a radical change, but unfortunately, it became necessary. I’m truly sorry for the inconvenience.

That said, I believe it was better to introduce this now rather than face even worse confusion down the road.

[h3]What you should know:[/h3]
Depending on where you discovered Lunar Eclipse, you may be using one of three different builds:
[list]
[*][b]Development[/b]
[*][b]Demo[/b]
[*][b]Early Access[/b] (available June 4th)
[/list]
Each of these builds can have a different world state. For example, if you save your game in the Development build, that save will reflect the Development version of the world. Loading that same save in the Early Access version could cause unintended behavior — some objects might be unexpectedly activated or deactivated. In the worst-case scenario, you could spawn in the middle of nowhere.

Previously, players could unknowingly do this, but now that the community is growing, I had to make a decision to solve the problem.

This new system allows me to keep all three versions of the game updated while minimizing the risk of save file conflicts.

Here’s how the loading menu looks from now on:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45015378/76caded8372addfc26493c730ea99ae20d2160d7.png[/img]

Also, since Lunar Eclipse is mostly puzzle-based, I’m sure many of you can breeze through the game again fairly quickly — though I’m still really sorry for the inconvenience.

Thanks so much for your understanding and support. It truly means a lot to me ❤️

[hr][/hr]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2953480/Lunar_Eclipse/

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.37
notes.content:
[b]Hey everyone![/b]

Today I’m excited to finally share a feature a lot of you have been asking for — full gamepad support is now live in Lunar Eclipse!

It took me about 25 full days (yes, weekends included) to make it all work properly — from rewriting UI interactions to updating every single menu. There's still a few rough edges here and there, so thanks in advance for your patience and understanding. I’ll keep polishing things in the upcoming updates! Let’s dive into what’s new:

[h3]Gamepad Support — it’s here![/h3]
[list]
[*]Full [b]native support for Xbox controllers[/b] has been added.
[*]Thanks to [b]Steam Input[/b], [b]PlayStation controllers[/b] (and probably others too!) should work automatically, even though they aren’t officially supported yet.[/list]
    ⚠️ Heads-up: If you run the game outside of Steam, only Xbox controllers will work by default. For other controllers, you’ll need third-party software.

[list]
[*]Right now there’s only Xbox-style button icons, but I’m looking into ways to add automatic layout detection or a manual layout selector in the settings.
[*]I also added a help field at the bottom of most menus to show which buttons do what. It switches automatically between gamepad and keyboard depending on what you pressed last.[/list]
   ⚠️ But! I still recommend sticking to one input method — juggling both might confuse the game (and your fingers :D).

[h3]Key Remapping for Gamepad[/h3]
The Controls tab in the settings menu now allows you to fully remap both keyboard and gamepad buttons. So feel free to customize the layout to whatever feels comfy for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45015378/84e186bc230aea87bf594a2ac9033ca2c1e94f6b.png[/img]

[h3]UI Changes & Improvements[/h3]
[b]Crafting Menu[/b] completely rebuilt to work smoothly with both keyboard and gamepad. It also just looks nicer now (I hope!) — let me know what you think.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45015378/abd8e7e2301225eff8cbc9b193285989bdeeb5e8.png[/img]

[h3]Outfits Tab Overhaul[/h3]
[list]
[*]The Outfits menu has been redesigned to match the new “collectible pieces” system.
[*]Now each individual clothing item (top, bottom, etc.) is collected and shown separately. Gotta collect 'em all!
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45015378/4f93d427c636b2c2b5214f5aafadf5a127217a10.png[/img]

[h3]Other Fixes & Improvements[/h3]
There’s also a whole bunch of small tweaks and fixes sprinkled throughout the game. I won't bore you with every tiny detail, but if something suddenly works better than before — it was probably in this patch :D

[h3]What’s Next?[/h3]
I’m slowly getting back to work on the third major area — it’s coming along nicely!
If all goes well, it should be ready in next two months for Steam and include:
[list]
[*]A new large zone: Living Rooms
[*]New puzzles to tease your brain
[*]New outfits (aiming for 3–4 new sets, we’ll see!)
[*]And more cool stuff
[/list]
Thank you so much for your continued support!
Our community is still small, but it means the world to me ❤️

I’m especially excited for the [b]Early Access[/b] launch on [b]June 4[/b] — it’s a big and important step for me as a developer, and I’ll keep doing my best to deliver the best experience possible.

I love [b]Lunar Eclipse[/b], and I hope you’ll enjoy the journey alongside me.

[hr][/hr]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2953480/Lunar_Eclipse/

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Coming to Early Access on June 4!
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

I’m excited to finally announce that Lunar Eclipse will launch in Early Access on [b]June 4, 2025[/b], on Steam!

This is a huge milestone, and I’m incredibly thankful for all your support, feedback, and kind words since the demo release. The Early Access version includes new content, improvements, and fixes - many of which were directly influenced by the community.

Here’s a quick recap of some of the most interesting additions since the first demo:

[h3]New Area: The Basement[/h3]
Explore a completely new location with fresh puzzles, additional exploration zones, new collectibles, and more intense zombie encounters.

[h3]New Outfit: Casual Set[/h3]
In the basement, you can find a new [b]craftable outfit[/b] consisting of a [b]sweater,[/b] [b]jeans[/b], [b]boots[/b], and [b]underwear[/b].
To craft it, you’ll need to gather materials dropped from enemies - so be ready to fight and scavenge.

[h3]Outfit Crafting System[/h3]
You can now [b]craft outfits[/b] using resources found in the world or looted from enemies.
Outfits are not only cosmetic but also help build immersion and allow you to customize Ealish’s look as you progress.

[h3]Expanded Settings Menu[/h3]
[list]
[*]Camera options: adjust sensitivity, inversion, and position
[*]Fully customizable keyboard controls
[*]New supported languages: [b]Russian[/b], [b]Ukrainian[/b], and [b]Simplified Chinese[/b]
[/list]
[h3]Narrative Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*]A large portion of the dialogue has been rewritten for better flow and stronger storytelling.
[*]New collectible note type: [b]audio recordings[/b] that reveal what happened while Ealish was asleep.
[/list]
[h3]Visual Upgrades[/h3]
[list]
[*]New enemy models have been added to improve visual variety and overall atmosphere.
[/list]
...and tons of other improvements and tweaks throughout the game!

Thank you again for your amazing support. I can’t wait to share more updates with you as we move toward the full release.

Don’t forget to [b]wishlist Lunar Eclipse on Steam[/b] and [b]follow the game[/b] to stay up to date!

[hr][/hr]

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.36
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

While working on gamepad support and reworking parts of the UI - particularly the graphics settings menu - I introduced a few bugs that affected how graphical settings were initialized, especially for players without existing save data.

This issue caused incorrect defaults to be applied to options like [b]Resolution Scale[/b], [b]Screen Resolution[/b], and other general graphics settings (such as [b]Shadow Quality,[/b] [b]Post-Processing Quality[/b], [b]Reflection Quality[/b], etc.).

The issue is now fixed, and everything should initialize correctly. You can continue playing normally.

Please note: Some parts of the UI might still look a bit clunky when using a gamepad. This is a temporary situation.

Once gamepad support is fully finished (hopefully before the Early Access launch), I’ll make a separate announcement dedicated to the new gamepad features, including the reworked crafting menu.

That’s all for now - thank you for your support! I’ll be back soon with more exciting news.

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.35
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

Today’s update is a relatively small one, but still meaningful. Just to give you a bit of context - I’m currently working hard on preparing the game for [b]Early Access next month[/b], which means lots of things are happening behind the scenes. Despite the workload, I’ve managed to push a few updates: [b]new language support[/b] and the [b]first steps toward full gamepad support[/b]. Let's go over everything!

[h3]Localization[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Ukrainian[/b] language has been added - this one is especially close to me, and I’m very happy to finally include it.
[*][b]Simplified Chinese[/b] is now also supported - if you're playing in this language, feel free to let me know if anything looks off or needs adjusting![/list]
And of course, if you'd like to see the game in other languages, don't hesitate to leave a comment. If there's enough interest, I'll be happy to add more localizations to my to-do list.

[h3]Save System[/h3]
[list]
[*]Added [b]4 additional save slots[/b] - the total number has now increased from 4 to [b]8[/b].[list]
   [*]This should give you more flexibility when experimenting or replaying certain parts of the game.[/list][/list]
Let me know if you'd like even more in the future - I’m open to expanding it further based on your needs.

[h3]Puzzles[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Added button press animations to keypads[/b], so you’ll now get clearer visual feedback when interacting with them. Small change, but it helps improve the feel of the puzzles.
[/list]
[h3]UI[/h3]
[list]
[*]Some [b]minor UI effects[/b] have been improved - previously they could get stuck during certain animations. This should now work more smoothly.
[/list]
[h3]Settings Menu[/h3]
[list]
[*]The [b]Display[/b] tab has been merged with the [b]Graphics[/b] tab. Now all your visual settings are in one place.
[*]A new [b]Key Binding[/b] tab has been added.
[*]Keyboard key bindings have been moved here from the [b]Controls[/b] tab.[list]
   [*]This is part of the ongoing work to support gamepads and improve overall navigation.
   [*]At the moment, only keyboard key remapping is functional - but gamepad remapping will be added once full controller support is ready.[/list][/list]
[h3]Outfit Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*]Fixed a few small [b]clipping issues[/b] with character outfits.[list]
   [*]Some visual artifacts may still appear due to technical limitations. I’ll keep working to resolve them where possible - thanks for your patience and understanding![/list][/list]
[h3]Gamepad Support (Work in Progress)[/h3]
[list]
[*]I have officially started working on [b]gamepad support[/b], starting with the [b]Xbox controller[/b].[list]
   [*]You [b]can’t control the character[/b] with the controller yet.
   [*]However, some menus (Main Menu, Options, Collectibles, Journal) should now work properly.
   [*]Dynamic button hints have also been added - they’ll now change based on whether you’re using a keyboard or controller.[/list]
[/list]
This is just the first step. I’m aiming to finish full gamepad support by the end of this month — I’ll keep you posted!

Thank you so much for your continued support - it really means a lot and keeps me motivated through the development process. If you have ideas, requests, or just want to say hi, feel free to leave a comment below.

More exciting updates are on the way, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.33
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

I'm happy to announce that [b]Lunar Eclipse[/b] has been updated to [b]version 0.33[/b]!
Although only the [b]Lunar Eclipse Demo[/b] is currently available on Steam, I'm actively working on the [b]Early Access[/b] version. Many of the improvements made to the full game also affect the demo, as they share the same core systems.

Below are the most important changes introduced in this update:

[h3]Dialogue[/h3]
[list]
[*]Some dialogues have been improved for a smoother narrative flow.
[/list]
[h3]Camera[/h3]
[list]
[*]The camera behavior has been reworked.
[*]You can now [b]slightly zoom/focus[/b] the camera using the [b]Right Mouse Button[/b], allowing for more precise inspection of the environment.
[*]If the character is crouching and starts an attack, they will automatically [b]stand up[/b] for the duration of the attack. You can press [b]C[/b] again to crouch after the attack ends.
[/list]
[h3]Camera Options[/h3]
Some players mentioned that the [b]default camera angle and distance[/b] didn’t feel comfortable for them. I really appreciate the feedback and want to make sure everyone can enjoy the game in a way that feels right.

So, based on those suggestions, I’ve added [b]two new camera configuration options[/b]:
[list]
   [*][b]Camera Height Offset[/b] – Adjust how high or low the camera is positioned behind the character.
   [*][b]Camera Distance[/b] – Control how close or far the camera is from the character.
[/list]
Both options can be found under the Gameplay tab in the settings menu. These changes should help improve visibility and overall comfort while playing.

[h3]Journal[/h3]
[list]
[*]The "[b]Reports[/b]" tab has been merged with "[b]Notes[/b]".
[*]A new tab called "[b]Audio Recordings[/b]" has been added.
[*]The journal now includes the following sections:[list]
    [*][b]Notes[/b]: Hints, technical documents, and brief descriptions.
    [*][b]Audio Recordings[/b]: Events that occurred while Ealish was asleep in the incubator - why there are zombies in the lab, why she slept for so long, and where everyone went.
    [*][b]Diaries[/b]: Insights into Ealish's childhood, lab staff members, their daily lives, and the purpose of the facility.[/list][/list]
[h3]Outfit[/h3]
[list]    
[*]A new outfit piece has been added: [b]Uniform E-1 Bra[/b].
[*]It can now be found in [b]Ealish’s wardrobe[/b] along with the rest of the outfit.
[/list]
[b]Important Note[/b]:
Due to technical limitations, the bra will [b]only appear correctly if you start a new game[/b].
I’m really sorry for the inconvenience this might cause. It’s something I’ll try to improve in the future, and I truly appreciate your understanding.

[h3]Collectibles[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Collectible plushies[/b] have been improved.
[*]They now appear in the player's [b]inventory[/b] in addition to the statistics tab. While they don't have functional use yet, their [b]descriptions provide insights[/b] into Ealish’s childhood.
[/list]

That’s all for now!
Thank you so much for supporting Lunar Eclipse.
Early Access is just around the corner, so stay tuned for more updates and don't miss the release!

[hr][/hr]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2953480/Lunar_Eclipse/

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.25
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

I’m actively working on the game, developing new zones and puzzles. Along with these additions, some mechanics are being refined, and the overall gameplay experience is improving. These changes also affect the Lunar Eclipse Demo. Below, I’ve highlighted the most significant updates that impact the demo.

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Fixed Bug:[/b] Improved the logic that allowed players to hold a button during dialogue, which could cause uncontrollable execution of game logic. This issue could disrupt both gameplay mechanics and UI functionality.
[*][b]Fixed Bug:[/b] Addressed an issue where pressing Tab and Esc simultaneously could cause the selection wheel to get stuck on the screen, requiring extra steps to unfreeze it. From now on, holding Tab and Esc together should no longer trigger this incorrect behavior.
[/list]
[h3]New Option: Camera Speed Stabilization[/h3]
[list]
[*]Some players experienced motion sickness due to camera rotation speed. I’ve added a new [b]Camera Speed Stabilization[/b] setting, which can be found under the Gameplay tab. Please read the description carefully to configure it properly.
[*]The default [b]Camera Speed Stabilization[/b] value has also been adjusted, making the camera more responsive to mouse movement by default.
[/list]
[h3]Other Improvements & Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Options:[/b] The default [b]Camera Field of View[/b] has been increased from [b]75[/b] to [b]80 degrees[/b].
[*][b]Translation:[/b] The Russian translation has been improved and is now [b]99% complete[/b] for the [b]Lunar Eclipse Demo[/b].
[*][b]Sounds:[/b] New environmental sounds have been added to make the world feel more immersive.
[*][b]Interactions:[/b] Improved camera behavior when interacting with objects. The camera should no longer clip into the character except in rare cases due to specific situations or human error.
[*][b]Inventory & Interactions:[/b][list]
    [*]Previously, players had to rely on the “[b]E[/b]” indicator to give an item to an interactive object. This sometimes led to confusion, as some players tried to apply items to any object displaying “[b]E[/b]”.
    [*]Now, the [b]inventory will open automatically[/b] when interacting with an object that actually requires an item, making the process more intuitive.[/list]
[/list]
[b]Thank you all for your support![/b]

Join the [b]Discord[/b] server to stay updated on development progress and get exclusive insights before [b]Lunar Eclipse[/b] enters Early Access this summer!

[hr][/hr]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2953480/Lunar_Eclipse/

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.24
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

I’m happy to announce that patch [b]0.24[/b] is now live! This update focuses on improving the beginning of the game, mainly refining the Lunar Eclipse Demo experience. Below are the most notable improvements since patch [b]0.23[/b]:

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Fixed a bug[/b] where zombies could still attack the player for a couple of seconds after being killed by Ealish. This issue has now been resolved.
[*][b]Fixed a bug[/b] that sometimes prevented players from skipping the first dialogue when starting a new game. I’ve improved the logic responsible for this, and players should no longer lose control during the opening dialogue.[/list]
[h3]Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Font Size Adjustment[/b]: Some players had difficulty reading in-game text and requested a larger font. The font size in the [b]Journal[/b] and [b]dialogues[/b] has been increased by [b]20-30%[/b]. I will continue monitoring feedback to make further adjustments if necessary.
[*][b]Puzzle Hint Improvement[/b]: The hint for the first puzzle (in the room with the incubator) has been improved. Players will now find a [b]clearer visual guide[/b] on the back of the incubator, making it easier to understand the steps needed to solve the puzzle.
[*][b]Ealish’s Drawing Update[/b]: The drawing hint for the locked shelf (where players need to find one of the cylinders for the treasure box) has been improved. The [b]numbers were removed, and colors were separated[/b] to make it easier to understand, especially for players unfamiliar with this type of game.
[/list]
[h3]Options & Settings[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Camera Field of View (FOV) Setting[/b]: Players can now adjust the [b]Camera FOV[/b] in the [b]Gameplay[/b] tab. Some players found the default FOV uncomfortable, so this option allows for customization to improve the experience. I plan to add more camera settings in future updates.
[*][b]New Language - Russian[/b]: Lunar Eclipse Demo has been [b]almost fully translated into Russian[/b]. There are still minor errors, but I am actively tracking and improving the translation. [b]From now on, languages can be selected in Options under the Gameplay tab[/b].[/list]
[h3]Puzzle Balancing[/h3]
I am closely reviewing feedback regarding puzzles. For now, I will not be adding multiple difficulty modes, as that would introduce unnecessary complexity to the game’s logic. Instead, I will adjust early-game puzzles to be more accessible for new players, while later puzzles will naturally increase in difficulty as players become more familiar with the mechanics and what to expect.

That’s all for now! I truly appreciate everyone who has played Lunar Eclipse so far and continues to support the game with passion and enthusiasm. I’m working hard to make it even better, so stay tuned for future updates!

[hr][/hr]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/2953480/Lunar_Eclipse/

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse - Update 0.23
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

The Lunar Eclipse demo has been updated from [b]0.2 to 0.23[/b]. Below are the most notable changes from the past week.

[h3]Resolution Scale[/h3]
[list]
[*]The default resolution scale has been adjusted from [b]80 to 70[/b] for a better experience. Some players may not be aware of this setting, so I’ve optimized it by default to improve performance without noticeable quality loss.
[*]Players can still manually increase this setting if they have high-performance hardware.
[/list]
[h3]Game Settings[/h3]
[list]
[*]The "[b]Other[/b]" tab has been removed, and its content has been moved to the "[b]Gameplay[/b]" tab.
[*]A new option to [b]toggle the in-game FPS counter[/b] has been added. You can find it in the "[b]Display[/b]" tab.
[*][b]Descriptions have been added[/b] to various parameters in the "[b]Graphics[/b]" and "[b]Display[/b]" tabs.
[*]Players can now [b]rebind puzzle-related buttons[/b]. To differentiate between categories, an additional "[b]Category Button[/b]" column has been introduced, currently supporting two categories: "[b]Game[/b]" and "[b]Puzzle[/b]".
[*]A new option has been added to [b]toggle Ealish’s avatar on or off[/b]. Some players might find the avatar distracting, so they now have the ability to disable it in the "[b]Gameplay[/b]" tab for a more immersive experience.
[/list]
[h3]Camera Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*]The player's camera has been improved, with additional logic implemented to address situations where the camera could clip through the character.
[*]This issue has not been fully resolved, and I will continue working on a more refined solution.
[/list]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Fixed a critical bug[/b] that prevented players from inserting items even when an interactive object was activated.
   [list]
   [*]Example: Previously, players could start interacting with [b]Ealish’s Box[/b], but the cylinders wouldn’t work if a [b]save event[/b] interrupted the interaction logic. This has now been fixed.[/list]
[*][b]Fixed an issue where players could insert items into interactable objects from a distance under specific circumstances.[/b]
   [list]
   [*]Example: If certain conditions were met, players could insert a cylinder into Ealish’s Box without directly interacting with it. Now, interaction must be initiated with the "[b]E[/b]" button.[/list]
[*][b]Fixed a bug affecting total playtime tracking.[/b]
   [list]
   [*]Under certain conditions, loading a game and saving again could cause the total playtime to [b]double, triple, or more[/b], depending on the initial session time.
   [*] This issue has now been corrected, but note that [b]loading an old save will reset the playtime to zero[/b] to ensure accuracy moving forward.[/list][/list]
[h3]Other Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*]The [b]environment[/b] has been adjusted to improve player experience, and some interactive objects have been fine-tuned.
[*]The [b]main menu[/b] has been slightly changed. [b]Ealish is no longer present in the menu[/b]. Instead, as the game evolves, the main menu will feature narrative scenes.
[*]The [b]code panel has been improved[/b]. Previously, if you stopped interacting with the panel, the digits would remain on the screen. Now, they will be [b]cleared as soon as you exit the interaction[/b].
[/list]
That’s all for now! I’m incredibly grateful to everyone who has played Lunar Eclipse and continues to support it with passion and love. I’ll keep working hard to make the game even better and more engaging - so stay tuned for future updates!

notes.title: Lunar Eclipse – Update 0.20
notes.content:
[b]Hello everyone![/b]

Over the past two weeks, a lot has been done, and the demo has been significantly improved. Lunar Eclipse Demo has been updated to version 0.2. Below, I’ll cover the most notable changes implemented since version 0.1, which was released on January 15, 2025.

[h3]Major changes from 0.1 (15.01.2025) to 0.15 (14.02.2025)[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Full combat system added[/b], including health, combat mechanics, damage, healing, and death.
[*] [b]The starting location has been completely reworked[/b] to better align with the main story.
[*] [b]New dialogues added[/b], and the beginning of the story has been refined to improve the narrative flow and Ealish’s journey.
[*] [b]New puzzles introduced[/b], better integrated into the story.
[*] [b]Significant improvements to game mechanics[/b] with new logical elements.
[*] [b]New loading screen system implemented[/b], improving the player experience after map loading. Players should no longer see textures loading in real-time or objects popping in.
[*] [b]Background music enhanced[/b], now playing more smoothly across the game and main menu for a better overall experience.
[*] [b]Numerous new environmental props added[/b] to enrich the game world.
[/list]
[h3]Major changes from 0.15 (14.02.2025) to 0.2[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]A new in-game guide system[/b] has been added. The guide will be displayed to players during gameplay. Additionally, a new "Guide" tab has been added to the Journal, allowing players to access all game-related information at any time.
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45015378/3d0c059236297babbe31264877fcdb1200bb62fa.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]Smoother UI animations[/b] added for the Journal window when reading notes, reports, diaries, and guides.
[*] [b]Options menu significantly improved for better usability[/b]:
   [list]        
         [*] Toggleable settings (e.g., On/Off) can now be continuously cycled for convenience.
         [*] Descriptions have been added for some settings to better explain their functionality.
         [*] The old "[b]Controls[/b]" tab has been replaced with "[b]Keyboard & Mouse[/b]".
         [*] [b]Keyboard and mouse configuration[/b] has been implemented:
         [list]
               [*] Players can now rebind primary action keys.
               [*] Mouse settings now allow for adjusting sensitivity and inverting the X or Y axis.
[/list] [/list] [*] [b]New zombie models introduced[/b], better reflecting the main story. The "[b]bold guy in the red shirt[/b]" will no longer be alone - he can now share his unfortunate fate with the rest of the lab staff!
[*] [b]Modular outfit system implemented[/b]. I have been working on this system since the early days of Lunar Eclipse, and I’m excited to announce that it is now functional.
    [list]
          [*] This system allows equipping individual clothing items separately - [b]shirts, skirts, boots, and more[/b].
          [*] While still a work in progress, the first outfit for Ealish is now fully modular, with [b]body, panties, and boots[/b] as separate components.
          [*] Additional outfits will be integrated as the game evolves, as they require careful refinement.
    [/list][/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45015378/a60f06b0a7a7c3b87fadc60a721eb84ab64e12b2.png[/img]

[h3]Other Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] [b]Fixed a Journal bug[/b] where the second page could get stuck when switching entries. This issue has now been resolved.
[*] [b]All UI windows can now be closed[/b] using Esc, E, or Right Mouse Button (RMB).
[*] [b]Improved the "Collectibles" tab[/b] in the Journal. Now, only statistics for collectibles that can actually be found at the moment will be displayed.
[*] [b]New visual hints added for UI buttons[/b], visible in menus like "Inventory" and "Storage." More hints will be added in future updates for better player convenience.
[*] [b]A new healing item has been placed in the map[/b] to help Ealish restore her health.
[*] [b]Various technical improvements[/b], including core enhancements to the Journal system, new puzzle elements, code optimization, and testing of new features.
[/list]
[h3]Puzzles[/h3]
Lunar Eclipse is a blend of exploration, puzzles, and adventure, with puzzles still playing a significant role in the experience. So I carefully design each one to be engaging but not overly difficult. My goal is to strike the right balance between puzzles, exploration, and combat.
[list]
[*] [b]Some puzzles have been slightly adjusted[/b] to enhance the overall player experience.
[*] [b]I am continuously gathering feedback[/b] to refine more complex puzzles in future updates.
[*] [b]I’m aware that some players find certain puzzles challenging[/b]. I am monitoring feedback and will make adjustments over time.
[/list]
[h3]Bugs & Feedback[/h3]
If you [b]encounter any bugs[/b], please don’t hesitate to report them in whatever way is most convenient for you. This will allow me to investigate and add the issue to my to-do list for future fixes and improvements.
